Add your phone number to your Business Profile to help customers reach you directly. This can improve your business's visibility on Google and build trust with potential customers.

![Add your phone number](https://storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/zlK5nFYiNTyjPMkzy0FmOoYCur5VNyT1JHw2)

1. [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2. Select **Edit profile**![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) **Contact**.
3. Next to “Phone number,” select Edit ![Edit pencil](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/YdpYLwumnJmx_u1Rf_yYxCbUsEcuV5VdfZLJzWUVn0xob_N_7Zrz-I9CSXl-Q0VMfOEJ=h36).
4. To set the country code, select your country.
5. Enter your phone number.
   - You don't have to add country code, parentheses, and dashes to phone numbers since they’re automatically formatted.
   - If you want to add additional phone numbers, select **Add phone number**.
6. Select **Save**.

**Tips:**

- In addition to your primary business phone number, you can add up to 2 more phone numbers. You can add mobile or landline numbers but fax numbers can’t be added.
- You can also hide your phone number on your Business Profile. [Learn how to hide your phone number](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617#phone).

# Let’s Grow Your Local Presence

Our team is here to answer your questions or help you get started.

![Blog Image](https://gmbpro.in//storage/131/68c95951985e7_google-business-profile-phone-number-verification.png)

## Google Business Profile Phone Number Verification: How to Verify & Display Your Number

Verifying your phone number on Google Business Profile is crucial to ensure customers can see and call your business directly from your listing. This verification process not only legitimizes your profile but also improves your local SEO and trustworthiness. A verified phone number means your contact details are confirmed by Google, which helps your business appear more reliably in local search results.

### Why Verifying Your Google Business Profile Phone Number Matters

A **Google Business Profile** with a verified phone number signals to both Google and customers that your business is legitimate and reachable. Here are a few key benefits of phone number verification:

**Builds Trust:** People tend to trust businesses that have verified information on Google. A confirmed phone number shows that you are a real business, which can make potential customers more confident in contacting you.

**Improves Local SEO Visibility:** Google is more likely to showcase businesses with verified details in local search results and Google Maps. A verified profile can help you rank higher or appear more frequently when users search for services you offer in your area.

**Ensures Easy Customer Contact:** When your phone number is verified and displayed on your profile, customers can conveniently call you with one click or tap. Accurate contact info means you won’t miss out on inquiries from interested customers.

On the flip side, if your number is not verified, Google might limit its visibility. Unverified or incorrect phone details could result in your number not showing up on your public listing at all. This not only hurts your credibility but also means potential customers can’t reach you, leading to lost opportunities. Therefore, verifying the phone number is a fundamental step in optimizing your Google My Business (Google Business Profile) presence and ensuring your listing works for you.

### How to Verify Your Google Business Profile Phone Number

Verifying by phone is one of the fastest ways to confirm your Google Business Profile. Google will send you a verification code via an automated call or text message that you need to enter in your profile. Follow these steps to verify your phone number:

**Sign in and Find Your Business:** Log in to your Google Business Profile account using the Google account that manages your listing. If you have multiple business profiles, select the correct business from the dashboard.

**Initiate Verification:** Click on the _Verify now_ or _Get verified_ button for your business. Google will present the available verification options. Choose Phone (or SMS) if it’s offered for your profile. (If phone verification isn’t offered, use the method Google provides – such as postcard or email.

**Receive the Code:** Google will send a 5–6 digit verification code to your business phone number. You might receive this code via a phone call (an automated voice will read it out) or as an SMS text message. Be ready to answer the call or check your texts so you can note the code.

**Enter the Code:** Once you have the code, enter it into the verification field on your Google Business Profile dashboard and submit. If the code is correct, Google will confirm that your number is now verified.

**Confirmation:** After submitting the code, Google may take a short time to process the verification. In many cases the verification is instant, but sometimes it could take a day or two for the status to update. You will receive a confirmation notification once your phone number is officially verified.

**Pro Tips:** Use a direct line for verification (avoid fax or extensions). Enter the number in international format (with the +country code) to prevent formatting issues. When requesting the code, ensure you can immediately answer the call or view the SMS, as verification codes can expire. If you don’t receive a code, double-check that your phone number is correct in your profile and request a new code. You can also try a different verification method if phone/SMS isn’t working.

### Ensuring Your Phone Number Shows on Your Profile

After completing verification, your phone number should display publicly on your Google Business Profile (on Search and Maps). If it’s not visible, try these steps:

**Display Setting:** Make sure you haven’t accidentally hidden your number. In your Business Profile settings, under Advanced settings, the _“Don't show”_ option for phone number should be turned off.

**Allow Time for Updates:** Sometimes Google takes a short time (a few hours or up to a day or two) to update your information after verification. Also double-check that your entire business listing is verified and not pending any other verification steps.

**Number Format & Consistency:** Ensure your phone number is entered in the correct format (include the country code, e.g. +1 or +91). The number on your Google profile should match the number on your website and other listings – consistency helps Google trust the info. Avoid using a phone number that’s also on another Google listing, as this can cause conflicts.

**Additional Verification :** In some cases, Google might keep your number in a verification stage (especially in regions with strict checks). If your number still isn’t showing, you may need to fill out Google’s [**Phone Number Verification**](https://gmbpro.in/services/gmb-profile-setup-and-verification) **Appeal** form or provide documentation to prove the number belongs to your business. This extra step helps Google confirm the number is legitimate.

[**Contact Support:**](https://gmbpro.in/contact-us) If you’ve tried the above and your number remains hidden, reach out to [Google Business Profile Support](https://gmbpro.in/contact-us) or post your issue on the community forums. Google’s support team can investigate if there's a technical issue or guide you on the next steps.

### Next Steps

Verifying and displaying your phone number on Google Business Profile is a simple step that yields significant benefits for your business. It ensures your business is reachable and trustworthy to both customers and Google. Don’t let an unverified or hidden phone line stand between you and potential customer calls.

At **GMBpro**, we offer professional support to maximize your presence on Google. Our services include [GMB Profile Setup and Verification](https://gmbpro.in/services/gmb-profile-setup-and-verification) to get your listing properly verified, [GMB Profile Optimization](https://gmbpro.in/services/gmb-profile-optimization) to improve rankings, and [GMB Analytics and Reporting](https://gmbpro.in/services/gmb-analytics-and-reporting) to monitor your performance. Feel free to explore all our services.

Have more questions? Check our [FAQ](https://gmbpro.in/faq) for common queries or [contact us](https://gmbpro.in/contact-us) for personalized assistance. You can also see how it works to learn about our process. With a verified phone number and an optimized Google Business Profile, you’ll be well-positioned to connect with more customers and grow your business online.

# Let’s Grow Your Local Presence

Our team is here to answer your questions or help you get started.

![Blog Image](https://gmbpro.in//storage/153/69130d3746b27_how-to-show-phone-number-on-google-my-business-profile.png)

## How to Show Your Phone Number on Google My Business Profile

Discover how to make your phone number visible on Google My Business and increase customer calls with verified, optimized profile settings.

Your phone number is one of the most important contact elements on your **Google My Business (GMB)** or **Google Business Profile (GBP)**. It’s what turns visibility into real leads.

If your number isn’t showing, or customers can’t click “Call,” you’re losing direct sales opportunities every day.

This guide explains exactly how to **show your phone number on your Google Business Profile**, why it sometimes disappears, and how to optimize your listing so that it ranks higher and converts better.

At [**GMBPro**](https://gmbpro.in/), we’ve helped hundreds of businesses fix hidden contact info, verify their listings, and appear in Google Maps’ top results.

### **1\. Why Google Sometimes Hides Your Phone Number**

There are several reasons your phone number may not be visible on your profile:

- Your business profile isn’t verified.
- Your number doesn’t match what’s on your website or directories (NAP inconsistency).
- Google’s system detected duplicate or spam listings.
- You selected a service area without a physical location, which limits display.
- Your listing violates Google’s business information guidelines.

Google’s algorithm prioritizes accurate and consistent information. Any mismatch between your business listings and website can cause the phone field to be suppressed.

### **2\. How to Add or Update Your Phone Number on Google My Business**

Follow these steps to make sure your number appears properly:

**Step 1:** Sign in to your **Google Business Profile Manager** at business.google.com.

**Step 2:** Select your business and click **Edit Profile** → **Contact Information**.

**Step 3:** Under “Phone number,” add your correct, local business number (avoid toll-free numbers if possible).

**Step 4:** Save your changes.

**Step 5:** Check your live profile on Google Search and Maps to confirm the number is visible.

Always use a local area code. Users trust numbers that appear geographically close to them, improving your call conversion rate.

### **3\. Ensure NAP Consistency Across the Web**

**NAP = Name, Address, Phone Number**

Google checks multiple sources to confirm your data is accurate. If your phone number differs across directories, social media, or your website, it can hurt your rankings and prevent display.

**How to fix it:**

- Audit all online listings (JustDial, IndiaMart, Yelp, Facebook, website).
- Use the exact same phone number format everywhere.
- Avoid using tracking or forwarding numbers unless properly linked with your main line.

Google My Business phone number, NAP consistency, how to fix phone number on Google Maps.

### **4\. Verify Your Business for Full Visibility**

Unverified profiles have limited visibility and restricted features. Without verification, your contact details may not show to customers.

**How to verify:**

- Google will send a postcard, email, or call with a verification code.
- Enter that code into your profile.
- Once verified, your phone number becomes public and clickable.

Voice assistants like Google Assistant only show verified listings when responding to “Call \[business name\] near me.”

### **5\. Avoid Common Mistakes That Hide Your Number**

Some simple errors can cause your number to vanish or fail to display properly:

- Using a call tracking number that doesn’t match your main listing.
- Adding personal numbers instead of business lines.
- Copying and pasting your number with spaces or special characters.
- Failing to update hours or address after a move.

**Fix:** Keep your GMB profile formatting clean and standardized.

Google My Business verification, Google Maps contact info, show phone number on GMB.

### **6\. Optimize for Local Ranking**

Once your phone number is visible, boost your [**local visibility**](https://gmbpro.in/services/local-seo-add-ons) so customers actually find your listing.

**Optimization Tips:**

- Add your service areas (city and district names).
- Include local keywords in your description (e.g., “plumber in Ahmedabad” or “digital marketing agency in Vadodara”).
- Get backlinks from regional directories and Google Maps citations.
- Collect genuine Google reviews that mention your location and services.

Local SEO for Google My Business, Google Maps visibility, Google Business optimization in India.

### **7\. Improve CTR and User Engagement (SXO Layer)**

To attract more calls, make your listing visually appealing and trustworthy.

**Enhance your click-through rate (CTR) by:**

- Adding professional photos (storefront, team, service area).
- Writing a concise, keyword-rich business description.
- Using the “Call Now” and “Message” CTAs.
- Posting weekly updates with local offers and news.

When users trust your listing, they engage more — which boosts your ranking.

Increase Google My Business engagement, optimize GBP profile for calls, improve CTR on Google Maps.

### **8\. Track and Analyze Your Google Business Performance**

Use [**Google Business Insights**](https://gmbpro.in/services/gmb-analytics-and-reporting) to measure what’s working:

- How many people found you on Search vs Maps.
- How many clicked “Call” or “Directions.”
- Which keywords customers used to find you.

Use this data to adjust your content, location keywords, and posting frequency.

Google’s AI-driven ranking favors businesses that show consistent engagement signals and data accuracy.

### **9\. When to Contact Google My Business Support**

If your phone number still isn’t showing after optimization:

- Contact Google Business Support via chat or email.
- Provide verification proof (photos, business license, utility bills).
- Ask for manual review of your listing.

Google’s support agents use internal visibility systems that rely on your account’s authenticity and consistency to restore contact visibility.

### **10\. How GMBPro Helps You Fix and Rank Higher**

At [**GMBPro**](https://gmbpro.in/), we specialize in:

- Fixing hidden or missing contact details.
- Full GMB optimization for visibility and lead generation.
- Review management and posting strategy.
- Geo keyword targeting for top Google Maps ranking.
- Monthly performance reporting and AI visibility tracking.

**Result:** Verified, optimized, and visible Google Business Profiles that bring daily customer calls.

### **Make Your Business Easy to Call and Easy to Find**

Your phone number is more than a contact field — it’s the bridge between your online visibility and real-world customers.

If your **Google My Business** listing isn’t showing your number, it’s not just a technical issue — it’s a missed opportunity.

Keep your profile verified, accurate, and active — or let **GMBPro** do it for you.

We’ll ensure your business is fully visible, contactable, and trusted on Google Maps and Search.

web.description: For a business listing on Google Business Profile, it's best to use a local phone number that directly reaches the specific business location.
web.markdown:
Are you looking to enhance your Google Business Profile but are unsure of the rules? Understanding Google Business Profile guidelines is crucial for boosting your online presence and avoiding penalties. In this article, we’ll walk you through the essential guidelines you need to know to create and maintain an effective profile to support your [local search optimization (LSO)](https://www.wearetg.com/services/local-search-optimization/) efforts and successfully rank your business.

### Key Takeaways

- A Google Business Profile enhances visibility and customer engagement, enabling businesses to manage their online presence across Google services.
- Accurate representation of information, including business hours, name, address, and phone number, is critical; errors can lead to profile suspension and diminished customer trust.
- Regular updates and compliance with Google’s guidelines are vital for maintaining a positive online reputation and maximizing the effectiveness of a Google Business Profile.

### What is Google Business Profile?

A Google Business Profile is a free resource that helps businesses establish their online presence across various Google platforms, including Search, Google Maps, and Shopping. As the initial point of contact for many potential customers, this virtual storefront plays an essential role in digital marketing strategies.

Providing current and precise information about your business not only draws more consumers but also promotes both web-based interaction and physical store visits. By optimizing a Google Business Profile effectively, companies improve their chances of appearing in local search engine results.

Beyond improving discoverability, Google Business Profiles are vital channels for companies to engage with clients by conveying updates and highlighting their offerings. Essentially operating as effective promotional tools without any cost implication, these profiles grant substantial benefits to businesses aiming to maximize their reach on the internet.

### Eligibility Criteria for Google Business Profile

Eligibility for a Google Business Profile requires businesses to have direct, in-person interactions with their customers during the hours they claim to operate. This stipulation is designed to allow only those businesses that either have a physical location or offer services at customer locations the ability to establish a profile, thus safeguarding the accuracy and trustworthiness of information provided.

A business can secure its spot on Google Business if it engages directly with local clients or companies, whether through an established storefront presence or not. Such accessibility enables various companies, including local businesses, service businesses, and even companies with multiple locations, to leverage the enhanced exposure and customer interaction facilitated by having a GBP.

On the other hand, companies operating exclusively via virtual channels or from post office boxes are ineligible for listing as official business profiles on Google. The reason for this restriction is twofold: preventing false business representations while ensuring people can genuinely engage with actual businesses. Some exceptions apply, like ATMs and seasonal ventures, which must adhere to specific standards such as permanent signage throughout the year.

Lastly, co-working spaces and delivery-only food establishments face unique guidelines before being featured. For instance, an enterprise stationed within a co-working space qualifies if unmistakable signs are posted alongside staff present during designated working hours. Similarly, stringent criteria exist when considering delivery-centric food operations for inclusion among legitimate commercial entities presented by Google.

### Accurate Representation of Business Information

Maintaining accurate business information on Google is essential. Businesses must display their name exactly as it appears in the physical, real-world establishment across all platforms to aid customers in recognizing and locating their business.

Incorrect details within a business profile or an erroneous business name may result in suspension from Google, thus affecting both visibility with potential customers and their trust. To maintain the accuracy of your Google Business Profile, routinely check elements such as the business name, address, and phone number for correctness. Utilizing tools like Semrush’s Listing Management can be effective in swiftly pinpointing and rectifying discrepancies in NAP (Name, Address, Phone) data.

It is important to consistently monitor and adhere to the guidelines set forth by Google since they are subject to change over time. Not following these specific individual guidelines could lead not only to modifications of your listed business information but also potentially lead to removal from Google listings altogether.

#### Business Name Guidelines

The business name on your Google Business Profile must match how it appears on physical signage, official websites, and legal paperwork. This uniformity across different mediums makes it easier for customers to identify the business. The key guideline here is that your Google Business Profile should mirror your official business name as recognized in non-digital contexts.

Presenting an incorrect or misleading business name can lead to customer confusion and potentially result in the suspension of the profile. To keep things clear and adhere to Google’s policies, refrain from adding superfluous details into the business name field. For professional service providers like physicians or attorneys, their given names, consisting of just a first and last name without additional descriptors, are all that should be included within their business’s listing.

While shortening a brand’s title might seem appealing for brevity purposes, utilizing its complete official moniker on GBP helps eliminate vagueness. Adhering to this approach guarantees accurate representation of your enterprise online, which plays an important role in establishing and sustaining a robust digital footprint.

#### Address and Service Area Rules

A correct business address maintains credibility and helps customers find your location easily. Google’s address rules are designed to prevent situations where customers show up at a nonexistent location, which can damage trust and reputation.

Service-area businesses, which do not require a physical address, must accurately define their separate service areas. These businesses should hide their address if there is no clear signage and specify the service area by entering streets, cities, and states served. Google Maps allows up to 20 service areas to be added to a profile, ensuring comprehensive coverage without creating multiple profiles for different areas. Typical service businesses can make great use of this.

Hybrid businesses operating with a storefront and service area must include both in one listing. Co-working spaces must meet specific requirements, such as having official signage and staff present during listed hours, to qualify as a business address. Following these guidelines maintains the integrity and visibility of a business’s online presence across various locations.

#### Phone Number and Website Requirements

For a business listing on Google Business Profile, it’s best to use a local phone number that directly reaches the specific business location. This not only improves search visibility but also ensures efficient communication with customers.

Including a direct link to the website allows customers to access accurate information swiftly and boosts the trustworthiness of the business profile.

### Choosing the Right Business Categories

Selecting appropriate business categories is crucial for the effectiveness of your Google Business Profile, as it informs Google about the nature of your services. Opting for a primary category that closely aligns with your core business can activate useful features specific to your industry, like booking buttons for eateries or scheduling options for beauty salons.

It’s important to keep additional categories relevant without saturating your profile. Choose only what’s essential to represent all aspects of your operations accurately. In cases where an exact match isn’t available, using a broader category may be advantageous.

Picking the right categories not only enhances visibility but also guarantees that when potential customers are searching, they find precisely what they’re looking for: your business. This intersection of user searches and your business profile is key to attracting more visitors and increasing customer engagement, making careful selection of categories an important aspect of effectively maintaining your Google Business Profile.

![Screenshot of the Enter a Business Category selection screen from Google Business Profile](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

### Setting and Managing Business Hours

Accurately providing regular business hours allows customers to know when they can patronize your establishment. Being transparent and clear with these timings is key in upholding trust and satisfaction among patrons, as well as meeting Google Business Profile guidelines.

It’s essential that businesses adjust their posted hours to align with seasonal fluctuations and noteworthy occasions, ensuring clientele remain well-informed of any adjustments to service availability. Designate exceptional operating periods during holidays or unique happenings so that expectations are managed appropriately.

Whenever there is a change in operational schedules, notifying customers helps them stay aware of any updates regarding accessibility. Should there be intervals within working days where the business ceases operation temporarily, these timeframes must be clearly and accessibly shared.

### Content Policies for Photos and Videos

Google Business Profile mandates that images and videos be high quality and relevant to your listing. Images must be in JPG or PNG format, have a size ranging from 10 KB to 5 MB, and be well lit, in focus, and free from excessive digital manipulation or filters.

For video content submitted to Google Business Profile, each clip should not exceed 30 seconds and should have a minimum resolution quality of 720p. Prioritizing top-notch, relevant visual media also improves the attractiveness of your business profile.

By adhering strictly to these prescribed standards regarding image and video submissions on Google Business Profile, you can significantly enhance your profile’s appeal while effectively showcasing what you offer potential customers.

### Posting Updates and Offers

Consistently updating your Google Business Profile with the latest offers and news can significantly boost your business’s online presence, attracting more virtual and physical traffic. Keeping up-to-date in an ever-evolving digital world is crucial for maintaining relevance.

Engage with customers by sharing timely posts about new developments, special promotions, or upcoming events on social media platforms. Crafting these updates makes your profile engaging and dynamic while ensuring that potential clients are well-informed about what’s happening. Remember to detail any promotional terms, including the validity period of specific deals.

To really captivate your audience’s attention, incorporate images, videos, and detailed descriptions into your updates. When posting about events, ensure you include essential details such as the name, location, and date alongside visually appealing multimedia content. Attach a ‘View offer’ button to promotion posts to streamline customer interaction with these specials, as well.

### Responding to Reviews

Addressing customer feedback is instrumental in strengthening the bond between your business and its customers. Reacting to reviews demonstrates that you value their opinions and are dedicated to enhancing your offerings.

Expressing gratitude for positive reviews acknowledges a customer’s endorsement while simultaneously reaffirming the positive aspects of their experience, thereby promoting repeat business. Quick replies signify a company’s commitment to accepting consumer input, further improving its reputation.

While confronting negative feedback may be daunting, it also offers a chance for development. Exhibiting understanding and readiness to address problems can leave a positive impression on prospective patrons by showcasing dedication towards consumer contentment. Keep responses professional and pertinent.

![A review from Timmermann Group's GBP with a response from the owner showing appreciation](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

### Compliance with GBP Policies

Adhering strictly to Google Business Profile policies is essential for keeping your profile visible and fully functional. If these guidelines are not followed, you could face serious repercussions such as limited access to certain features or even suspension of your business profile.

If any content on your profile goes against established policies, it may negatively affect how your business appears online. To prevent these types of penalties from occurring, it’s critical to observe Google’s rules closely. Not only do these guidelines help you improve the reach of your business’s digital presence, but they also improve the user experience of potential customers.

### Summary

To thrive online, businesses must keep their Google Business Profile accurate and fully optimized. This entails complying with eligibility criteria and ensuring that all business details are precisely depicted on the profile. Managing your GBP is key to improving visibility and engaging customers effectively. Consistently updating business hours, selecting appropriate categories, and following guidelines for photo and video content contribute significantly to a strong web presence.

Adhering to these practices not only makes businesses appear more credible but also enhances their competitiveness in local search results. It’s imperative to follow Google’s policies as failing to do so can result in harsh outcomes like profile suspension or limited access. Strict adherence is required without compromise. By remaining aware and vigilant, companies can maximize the benefits offered by their Google Business Profile in gaining new customers while maintaining current ones.

Mastering your Google Business Profile might be complex, but the advantages are substantial. Compliance with established guidelines will ensure your enterprise stands out amidst digital competition, capturing customer attention while building enduring connections.

* * *

#### Is Your Google Business Profile Helping You Rank — or Holding You Back?

Your Google Business Profile isn’t just a listing. It’s one of the most powerful local ranking tools you have. But small mistakes in categories, service areas, naming, or policy compliance can quietly hurt your visibility. If you’re unsure whether your GBP is fully optimized — or you want to improve rankings, engagement, and local conversions — let’s take a strategic look at it together. [![Schedule a Consultation button](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.wearetg.com/contact)

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is a Google Business Profile?

A Google Business Profile is a free tool from Google that allows businesses to share information and manage how they appear across Google platforms, such as Google Search, Google Maps, and Google Shopping. It helps you control your business information, engage with customers through reviews and messages, share updates, and showcase your products or services, all in one place. An optimized profile improves local visibility and makes it easier for potential customers to find and connect with your business.

#### Who is eligible for a Google Business Profile?

To be eligible for a Google Business Profile, your business must engage with customers in person during operating hours, whether at a physical location or by traveling to meet them.

However, online-only businesses or those operating from a P.O. box do not qualify.

#### How do I ensure my business information is accurate?

To ensure your business information is accurate, regularly verify your Google Business Profile and check for discrepancies in your name, address, and phone number (NAP).

Utilizing tools like Semrush’s Listing Management can effectively help identify and rectify NAP inconsistencies.

#### What are the guidelines for posting photos and videos?

To ensure a compelling business profile, photos should be in JPG or PNG format, clear, and well-lit, while videos must not exceed 30 seconds and should have a resolution of 720p or higher.

Following these guidelines will enhance the quality and relevance of your content, as well as improve the user experience of potential customers.

#### How should I respond to negative reviews?

Responding to negative reviews with empathy and a commitment to resolving issues is essential for positively influencing potential customers. Always maintain courtesy and relevance in your responses while refraining from sharing personal information about the reviewer.

The [guidelines for representing your business on Google](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) are like the “Bible” of Google Business Profiles (GBP). They are referred to and studied more than any other article in the [GBP help center](https://support.google.com/business#topic=4596754).

According to Google:

> To maintain high quality information on Google, follow this list of guidelines for local businesses. These guidelines can help you avoid common problems, including changes to your information or, in some cases, removal of your business information from Google.

In other words, the guidelines inform us of what we need to look for, and look out for, as a business profile manager, if we want to stay in Google’s good graces.

We highly recommend reading the guidelines at least once per year since Google is constantly modifying them.

Here are the highlights from the guidelines that we have found to be the most critical to be aware of.

Guidelines for Representing Your Business on Google - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[Guidelines for Representing Your Business on Google](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GmBnPluaVhk) [Sterling Sky Inc](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCGtqz4Xm5F76lHnSR88TcXQ)

Sterling Sky Inc113K subscribers

[Watch on](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GmBnPluaVhk)

### Business Name

We know that the [business name](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/keyword-stuffing-gmb-name/) is a ranking factor. Here is what Google states about the business name:

> To help customers find your business online, accurately represent your business name. Your name should reflect your business’s real-world name, as used consistently on your storefront, website, stationery, and as known to customers.

### Address

Google’s worst nightmare is customers showing up at an address on the map and the business isn’t there. Getting the address right and following the rules is critical. These are the most important things to remember.

1. P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations aren’t acceptable.
2. Create your Business Profile for your actual, real-world location.
3. Businesses showing their address on Google should maintain permanently fixed signage of their business name at the address.
4. If your business rents a physical mailing address but doesn’t operate out of that location, also known as a virtual office, that location isn’t eligible for a Google Business Profile.

### Service Area Businesses

The address guidelines above are for brick-and-mortar businesses. But what about [SAB’s](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/local-search-sabs/)? Here’s what Google has to say.

1. Service-area businesses, or businesses that serve customers at their locations, should have one profile for the central office or location with a designated service area.
2. Service-area businesses can’t have a [Google Business Profile virtual office](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/google-business-profile-virtual-office-guidelines/) address unless that office is staffed during regular business hours, which must be accurately reflected as part of your [Google business hours](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/google-business-profile-hours/).
3. If you have different locations for your service business, with separate service areas and separate staff at each location, you’re allowed one profile for each location.
4. The boundaries of your profile’s overall service area shouldn’t extend farther than about 2 hours of driving time from where your business is based.

### Website & Phone Number

Your website and phone number are how customers get ahold of you. Google wants to make sure that they are listed correctly.

1. Provide a phone number that connects to your individual business location, or provide a website that represents your individual business location.
2. Use a local phone number instead of a central call center helpline number whenever possible.
3. Do not provide phone numbers or URLs that redirect or “refer” users to landing pages or phone numbers other than those of the actual business, including pages created on social media sites.

### Categories

Getting your categories right is one of the most critical parts of a successful Google Business Profile. Here’s what Google says.

1. Use as few categories as possible to describe your overall core business from the provided list.
2. Do not use categories solely as keywords or to describe attributes of your business.
3. Select categories that complete the statement, “This business _IS_ a…” rather than “this business _HAS_ a…” The goal is to describe your business holistically rather than a list of all the services it offers, products it sells, or amenities it features.

# Guidelines for Chains, Departments, & Practitioners

Near the end of the guidelines, Google has a dedicated section for chains, departments, and practitioner listings. Here are the highlights.

### Chains

1. Maintain consistent names and categories across all of your business locations to help customers quickly identify your business on Google Maps and search results.
2. All business locations within the same country must have the same name for all locations.
3. All locations of a business must share the one category that best represents the business.
4. Virtual food brands are permitted with conditions.
5. If your business location combines two or more brands, do not combine the brand names into a single Business Profile. Instead, pick one brand’s name for the Business Profile. If the brands operate independently, you may use a separate profile for each brand at this location.

### Departments

1. Departments within businesses, universities, hospitals, and government institutions may have their own Business Profiles on Google.
2. [Auto dealers](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9074290) and [healthcare providers](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9074290) have specific and separate guidelines.
3. Publicly-facing departments that operate as distinct entities should have their own page.
4. The exact name of each department must be different from that of the main business and that of other departments.
5. Typically, such departments have a separate customer entrance and should each have distinct categories. Their hours may sometimes differ from those of the main business.

### Practitioners

1. An individual practitioner is a public-facing professional, typically with their own customer base. Doctors, dentists, lawyers, financial planners, and insurance or real estate agents are all individual practitioners.
2. Business Profiles for practitioners may include title or degree certification (for example Dr., MD, JD, Esq., CFA).
3. An individual practitioner should create their own dedicated Business Profile if:
   - They operate in a public-facing role. Support staff should not create their own Business Profiles.
   - They can be contacted directly at the verified location during stated hours.
4. A practitioner shouldn’t have multiple Business Profiles to cover all of their specializations.
5. Sales associates or lead generation agents for corporations aren’t individual practitioners and aren’t eligible for a Business Profile.
6. If the practitioner is one of several public-facing practitioners at this location:
   - The organization should create a Business Profile for this location, separate from that of the practitioner.
   - The title of the Business Profile for the practitioner should include only the name of the practitioner, and shouldn’t include the name of the organization.
7. If a practitioner is the only public-facing practitioner at a location and represents a branded organization, it’s best for the practitioner to share a Business Profile with the organization. Create a single Business Profile, named using the following format: \[brand/company\]: \[practitioner name\].

# So What?

Keep in mind that these are guidelines. Google seems to intentionally avoid the word _rules_. Keeping an eye on the guidelines and understanding them should allow you to have a better understanding of what Google thinks is best for their users (and your customers).

With that said, in addition to reading what Google writes, always watch to see what Google does in the wild. That is the key to success.
